text.p: Kenya's Paul Tergat, the reigning world cross country champion and Olympic 10,000m silver medallist, announced that 1997 is likely to be his last year as a serious track athlete.
"After running everything from 3,000m to 10,000m, the year after next I will switch to the marathon," said the 27 year old runner. "I want to finish my career as a marathon runner."
Tergat was speaking on Sunday in Brussels after winning the opening round of the 1996/1997 International Amateur Athletic Federation World Cross Challenge.

He said he had constantly been asked when he would attempt the 26.2 mile (42km) event after he ran 58 minutes 51 seconds for the half-marathon in Milan, Italy, on March 30. He had not made up his mind until recently.
His run in Milan was thought to be a world best by nearly a minute until the course was found to be 48 metres short. But it is still widely regarded as the best performance over the distance.
